subject: math
title: Adding and Subtracting to 100: Number Lines, Regrouping and Mental Math
seo_title: Grade 2 Math Adding and Subtracting to 100 Worksheets (BC Curriculum, Free, Answer Key)
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 math worksheets on adding and subtracting to 100: jumps on a number line, regrouping with base ten blocks, mental math, estimating and checking, and word problems about salmon counts and a school book fair. 100 questions with an answer key, following the BC curriculum.
key_big: Add tens to tens and ones to ones. Regroup when you need to.
key_sub: 37 + 25: jump +20 to 57, then +3 to 60 and +2 to 62. For 54 − 18 there are not enough ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 14 − 8 = 6 and 4 − 1 = 3, so 36.
body_html:
The idea: tens with tens, ones with ones

A 2-digit number has tens and ones. 46 is 4 tens and 6 ones. Add tens to tens. Add ones to ones.

Number sentenceAnswerWhat changes
46 + 3076the tens: 4 + 3 = 7
46 + 349the ones: 6 + 3 = 9
78 − 4038the tens: 7 − 4 = 3

Jump on an open number line

Start at the first number. Jump the tens. Then jump the ones. Jumping to the next ten makes it easier.

Subtract with regrouping

Sometimes there are not enough ones to take away. Regroup 1 ten as 10 ones.

Mental math: next ten and friendly numbers

Next ten: fill up to the next ten first. 46 + 7: 46 + 4 = 50, then 50 + 3 = 53.

Friendly number

What is 49 + 26?

49 is close to 50. 50 + 26 = 76. You added 1 too many, so take away 1: 76 − 1 = 75.

Answer: 75

Estimate and check

Before you add, find the closest tens. Your answer should be close to the estimate. To check a subtraction, add back what you took away.

Estimate

What is 48 + 25?

48 is close to 50. 25 is close to 30. 50 + 30 = 80. The exact answer is 73. 73 is close to 80, so it makes sense.

Answer: 73

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Not regrouping: 54 − 18 = 444 − 8 cannot be done. Regroup 1 ten: 14 − 8 = 6. Answer: 36
Not regrouping: 37 + 26 = 537 + 6 = 13 ones is 1 ten and 3 ones. Answer: 63
Adding tens to ones: 46 + 30 = 4930 is 3 tens. Add it to the tens: 76
Writing tens and ones side by side: 48 + 25 = 613Add the parts: 60 + 13 = 73

faq.q: What does Grade 2 learn about adding and subtracting in the BC math curriculum?
faq.a: In the BC curriculum, Grade 2 students add and subtract to 100. They use number lines, base ten blocks and mental math strategies, and they build on facts to 20.

faq.q: What mental math strategies do Grade 2 students use?
faq.a: Common strategies are jumping to the next ten (46 + 7 = 50 + 3), using doubles (23 + 24 is 1 more than 46) and using a friendly number (49 + 26 = 50 + 26 − 1 = 75).

faq.q: What is regrouping in Grade 2 subtraction?
faq.a: Regrouping means trading 1 ten for 10 ones when there are not enough ones. For 54 − 18, 54 becomes 4 tens and 14 ones, so the answer is 36.

faq.q: How can my child check an addition or subtraction answer?
faq.a: First estimate with the closest tens: 48 + 25 is about 50 + 30 = 80. Then check a subtraction by adding back: 62 − 25 = 37 because 37 + 25 = 62.

sets.title: Add tens and ones: jump on a number line

items.e: 30 is 3 tens. Add the tens: 4 tens + 3 tens = 7 tens. The ones stay the same. 46 + 30 = 76.

items.q: Count on by tens. What is 24 + 30?
items.e: Count on 3 tens from 24: 34, 44, 54. The ones stay the same. 24 + 30 = 54.

items.q: Count back by tens. What is 83 − 40?
items.e: Count back 4 tens from 83: 73, 63, 53, 43. The ones stay the same. 83 − 40 = 43.

items.q: What is 10 more than 58?
items.e: 10 more means 1 more ten. 5 tens become 6 tens. The ones stay the same: 68.

items.q: What is 10 less than 64?
items.e: 10 less means 1 less ten. 6 tens become 5 tens. The ones stay the same: 54.

items.q: Count on by tens. What is 29 + 50?
items.e: 50 is 5 tens. Add the tens: 2 tens + 5 tens = 7 tens. The ones stay the same. 29 + 50 = 79.

items.q: What is 13 + 40?
items.e: 40 is 4 tens. Add the tens: 1 ten + 4 tens = 5 tens. The ones stay the same. 13 + 40 = 53.

items.q: What is 45 − 20?
items.e: 20 is 2 tens. Take away the tens: 4 tens − 2 tens = 2 tens. The ones stay the same. 45 − 20 = 25.

items.q: Jump the tens, then the ones. What is 34 + 43?
Jump the tens, then the ones. What is 27 + 52?
Start at 42. Jump forward 30, then 6. Where do you land?
Jump the tens, then the ones. What is 53 + 25?
Jump back the tens, then the ones. What is 69 − 24?
Jump back the tens, then the ones. What is 78 − 45?
What is the missing jump?
items.e: From 46 to 76, the tens digit goes from 4 to 7. That is 3 tens, so the jump is +30. Check: 46 + 33 = 79.

items.q: Which number sentence does the number line show?
items.e: It starts at 28. It jumps +50 and +7. 50 + 7 = 57, so it shows 28 + 57 = 85.

items.q: Jump to the next ten. What is 37 + 27?
Jump to the next ten. What is 48 + 37?
Jump back to the ten. What is 65 − 28?
Find the missing number: 37 + ? = 77
items.e: The ones stay at 7. The tens go from 3 to 7. That is 4 tens: 40. Check: 37 + 40 = 77.

sets.title: Subtract with regrouping using base ten blocks

items.q: The blocks show 54. You need to take away 18. There are not enough ones. What do you do?
items.e: 54 has only 4 ones. You need to take away 8. Regroup 1 ten as 10 ones. Then there are 14 ones. Doing 8 − 4 instead is a common mistake.

items.q: You regroup 1 ten in 54. What does 54 look like now?
items.e: Take 1 ten from the 5 tens: 4 tens are left. The 10 ones join the 4 ones: 14 ones. So 54 = 4 tens and 14 ones. Check: 40 + 14 = 54.

items.q: 42 − 17. 1 ten was regrouped as 10 ones. Now there are 3 tens and 12 ones. 17 is crossed out. What is 42 − 17?
items.e: 42 has only 2 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 3 tens and 12 ones. Ones: 12 − 7 = 5. Tens: 3 − 1 = 2. 42 − 17 = 25.

items.q: 63 − 25. 1 ten was regrouped as 10 ones. Now there are 5 tens and 13 ones. 25 is crossed out. What is 63 − 25?
items.e: 63 has only 3 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 5 tens and 13 ones. Ones: 13 − 5 = 8. Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. 63 − 25 = 38.

items.q: 75 − 38. 1 ten was regrouped as 10 ones. Now there are 6 tens and 15 ones. 38 is crossed out. What is 75 − 38?
items.e: 75 has only 5 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 6 tens and 15 ones. Ones: 15 − 8 = 7. Tens: 6 − 3 = 3. 75 − 38 = 37.

items.q: 34 − 16. 1 ten was regrouped as 10 ones. Now there are 2 tens and 14 ones. 16 is crossed out. What is 34 − 16?
items.e: 34 has only 4 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 2 tens and 14 ones. Ones: 14 − 6 = 8. Tens: 2 − 1 = 1. 34 − 16 = 18.

items.q: 81 − 47. 1 ten was regrouped as 10 ones. Now there are 7 tens and 11 ones. 47 is crossed out. What is 81 − 47?
items.e: 81 has only 1 one, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 7 tens and 11 ones. Ones: 11 − 7 = 4. Tens: 7 − 4 = 3. 81 − 47 = 34.

items.q: 52 − 7. 1 ten was regrouped as 10 ones. Now there are 4 tens and 12 ones. 7 is crossed out. What is 52 − 7?
items.e: 52 has only 2 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 4 tens and 12 ones. Ones: 12 − 7 = 5. 4 tens are left. 52 − 7 = 45.

items.q: 80 − 36. 1 ten was regrouped as 10 ones. Now there are 7 tens and 10 ones. 36 is crossed out. What is 80 − 36?
items.e: 80 has 0 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 7 tens and 10 ones. Ones: 10 − 6 = 4. Tens: 7 − 3 = 4. 80 − 36 = 44.

items.q: Simran says 54 − 18 = 44. What mistake did she make?
items.e: In the ones, Simran took 4 from 8. But it must be 4 − 8, and you cannot take 8 from 4. Regroup: 14 − 8 = 6 and 4 − 1 = 3. So 54 − 18 = 36. Her mistake: she did 8 − 4.
62 has only 2 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 5 tens and 12 ones. Ones: 12 − 8 = 4. Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. 62 − 28 = 34.

items.q: What is 93 − 47?
items.e: 93 has only 3 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 8 tens and 13 ones. Ones: 13 − 7 = 6. Tens: 8 − 4 = 4. 93 − 47 = 46.
60 has 0 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 5 tens and 10 ones. Ones: 10 − 5 = 5. Tens: 5 − 3 = 2. 60 − 35 = 25.

items.q: What is 57 − 38?
items.e: 57 has only 7 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 4 tens and 17 ones. Ones: 17 − 8 = 9. Tens: 4 − 3 = 1. 57 − 38 = 19.
84 has only 4 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 7 tens and 14 ones. Ones: 14 − 6 = 8. Tens: 7 − 5 = 2. 84 − 56 = 28.

items.q: What is 46 − 27?
items.e: 46 has only 6 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 3 tens and 16 ones. Ones: 16 − 7 = 9. Tens: 3 − 2 = 1. 46 − 27 = 19.

items.q: What is 71 − 8?
items.e: 71 has only 1 one, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 6 tens and 11 ones. Ones: 11 − 8 = 3. 6 tens are left. 71 − 8 = 63.

items.q: What is 91 − 64?
items.e: 91 has only 1 one, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 8 tens and 11 ones. Ones: 11 − 4 = 7. Tens: 8 − 6 = 2. 91 − 64 = 27.

items.q: Find the missing number: 54 − ? = 36
Which subtraction needs regrouping?
items.e: In 64 − 27, there are only 4 ones. You need to take away 7, so regroup 1 ten. In the others, the top ones digit is big enough.

sets.title: Mental math: next ten, doubles and friendly numbers

items.q: You want to find 46 + 7. How many does 46 need to make 50?
items.e: 46 + 4 = 50. So add 4 first. 7 is 4 + 3, so then add 3 more: 50 + 3 = 53.

items.q: Jump to the next ten. What is 58 + 7?
Which one makes 50?
items.e: 3 + 7 = 10, so 43 + 7 = 50. The others make 51, 49 and 51.

items.q: Jump back to the ten. What is 63 − 5?
Use a double. 40 + 40 = 80. What is 40 + 39?
items.e: 39 is 1 less than 40. So 40 + 39 is 1 less than 80: 79.

items.q: Make a ten. What is 37 + 5?
items.e: Make the next ten. 37 + 3 = 40. Then add the rest: 40 + 2 = 42.

items.q: Make a ten. What is 28 + 6?
items.e: Make the next ten. 28 + 2 = 30. Then add the rest: 30 + 4 = 34.

items.q: Make a ten. What is 65 + 8?
items.e: Make the next ten. 65 + 5 = 70. Then add the rest: 70 + 3 = 73.

items.q: Make a ten. What is 27 + 15?
49 is close to 50. 50 + 26 = 76. Now take away 1. What is 49 + 26?
items.e: You added 1 too many when you used 50. Take it away: 76 − 1 = 75. (76 forgets to take away 1. 77 adds 1 instead.)

items.q: Use a friendly number. What is 19 + 24?
items.e: 19 is 1 less than 20. 20 + 24 = 44. Take away 1: 43.

items.q: Use a friendly number. What is 29 + 17?
items.e: 29 is 1 less than 30. 30 + 17 = 47. Take away 1: 46.

items.q: 38 is 2 less than 40. What is 38 + 15?
items.e: 40 + 15 = 55. You added 2 too many, so take away 2: 55 − 2 = 53. (55 forgets to take away 2.)

items.q: Which is the same as 27 + 9?
items.e: 9 is 1 less than 10. Add 10, then take away 1: 27 + 10 − 1 = 36.

items.q: Add 10, then take away 1. What is 33 + 9?
items.e: 33 + 10 = 43. You added 1 too many, so take away 1: 43 − 1 = 42. (43 forgets to take away 1.)

items.q: Which is the same as 35 + 19?
items.e: 19 is 1 less than 20. Add 20, then take away 1: 35 + 20 − 1 = 54.

items.q: Take away 10, then add 1. What is 42 − 9?
items.e: 42 − 10 = 32. You took away 1 too many, so add 1: 32 + 1 = 33. (47 takes 2 from 9 instead of 9 from 2.)

items.q: Take away 20, then add 1. What is 60 − 19?
items.e: 60 − 20 = 40. You took away 1 too many, so add 1: 40 + 1 = 41. (39 takes away 1 more instead of adding it back.)

items.q: Use a double. 23 + 23 = 46. What is 23 + 24?
items.e: 24 is 1 more than 23. So 23 + 24 is 1 more than 46: 47.

items.q: Use a double. 16 + 16 = 32. What is 16 + 17?
items.e: 17 is 1 more than 16. So 16 + 17 is 1 more than 32: 33.

items.q: Which ten is 37 closest to?
items.e: 37 is between 30 and 40. It is closer to 40.

items.q: Which ten is 53 closest to?
items.e: 53 is between 50 and 60. It is closer to 50.

items.q: Which ten is 72 closest to?
items.e: 72 is between 70 and 80. It is closer to 70.

items.q: Which ten is 28 closest to?
items.e: 28 is between 20 and 30. It is closer to 30.

items.q: Which ten is 84 closest to?
items.e: 84 is between 80 and 90. It is closer to 80.

items.q: Which ten is 61 closest to?
items.e: 61 is between 60 and 70. It is closer to 60.

items.q: Estimate. 39 + 22 is about how much?
items.e: 39 is close to 40. 22 is close to 20. 40 + 20 = 60.

items.q: Estimate. 48 + 31 is about how much?
items.e: 48 is close to 50. 31 is close to 30. 50 + 30 = 80.

items.q: Estimate. 62 + 27 is about how much?
items.e: 62 is close to 60. 27 is close to 30. 60 + 30 = 90.

items.q: Estimate. 63 − 37 is about how much?
items.e: 63 is close to 60. 37 is close to 40. 60 − 40 = 20.

items.q: Estimate. 71 − 18 is about how much?
items.e: 71 is close to 70. 18 is close to 20. 70 − 20 = 50.

items.q: Estimate. 41 + 28 is about how much?
items.e: 41 is close to 40. 28 is close to 30. 40 + 30 = 70.

items.q: Estimate first: 54 − 27 is about 50 − 30 = 20. What is 54 − 27?
items.e: 54 has only 4 ones, so regroup: 4 tens and 14 ones. 14 − 7 = 7. 4 − 2 = 2. 54 − 27 = 27. 27 is close to 20, so it makes sense.

items.q: Estimate first: 27 + 44 is about 30 + 40 = 70. What is 27 + 44?
items.e: Tens: 20 + 40 = 60. Ones: 7 + 4 = 11. 60 + 11 = 71. 71 is close to 70, so it makes sense.

items.q: Estimate first. Which answer to 48 + 25 makes sense?
items.e: 48 + 25 is about 50 + 30 = 80. Only 73 is close to 80. 613 writes 6 tens and 13 ones side by side. 23 subtracts. 55 adds the tens as ones.

items.q: Noah says 64 − 27 = 43. He estimates 60 − 30 = 30. What should he think?
items.e: 43 is far from 30, so 43 is too big. Noah did 7 − 4 in the ones. Regroup: 14 − 7 = 7 and 5 − 2 = 3. 64 − 27 = 37.

items.q: 62 − 25 = 37. Which addition checks the answer?
items.e: Add the answer and the number you took away. You should get back to the start: 37 + 25 = 62.

items.q: 46 + 37 = 83. Which subtraction checks the answer?
items.e: Take one part away from the total. You should get the other part: 83 − 37 = 46.

items.q: Jasleen says 53 − 16 = 43. She checks: 43 + 16 = 59. Is she right?
items.e: The check must give back 53. It gives 59, so she is not right. 53 − 16 = 37.

items.q: Which addition checks 80 − 26 = 54?
items.e: Add the answer and the number you took away: 54 + 26 = 80. You get back to 80.

sets.title: Word problems: salmon counts and the school book fair

items.q: On a field trip to the river, Liam’s class counts 34 salmon in the morning and 25 salmon after lunch. How many salmon do they count?
items.e: The bar model shows two parts. Find the whole, so add. Tens: 30 + 20 = 50. Ones: 4 + 5 = 9. 50 + 9 = 59.

items.q: At the school book fair, 27 students buy a book on Monday. 18 students buy a book on Tuesday. How many students buy a book?
items.e: The bar model shows two parts. Find the whole, so add. Tens: 20 + 10 = 30. Ones: 7 + 8 = 15. 15 ones is 1 ten and 5 ones. 30 + 15 = 45.

items.q: The book fair has 64 picture books. Students buy 28 of them. How many picture books are left?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. 64 has only 4 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 5 tens and 14 ones. Ones: 14 − 8 = 6. Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. 64 − 28 = 36.

items.q: A Grade 2 class raises salmon in a tank at school. They have 72 baby salmon. They let 27 go in the creek. How many baby salmon are still in the tank?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. 72 has only 2 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 6 tens and 12 ones. Ones: 12 − 7 = 5. Tens: 6 − 2 = 4. 72 − 27 = 45.

items.q: Which number sentence finds the missing part?
items.e: The whole is 65. One part is 29. Take the part away from the whole: 65 − 29 = ?. The missing part is 36.

items.q: In the Terry Fox Run, 37 Grade 2 students and 46 Grade 3 students ran. How many students ran?
items.e: The bar model shows two parts. Find the whole, so add. Tens: 30 + 40 = 70. Ones: 7 + 6 = 13. 13 ones is 1 ten and 3 ones. 70 + 13 = 83.

items.q: There are 53 bald eagles by the river. 17 eagles fly away. How many eagles are still by the river?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. 53 has only 3 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 4 tens and 13 ones. Ones: 13 − 7 = 6. Tens: 4 − 1 = 3. 53 − 17 = 36.

items.q: Arjun has $20 at the book fair. He buys a book for $12. How much money does he have left?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. 20 has 0 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 1 ten and 10 ones. Ones: 10 − 2 = 8. Tens: 1 − 1 = 0. 20 − 12 = 8.

items.q: Mei read 53 pages. Owen read 38 pages. How many more pages did Mei read?
items.e: How many more means find the difference, so subtract. 53 has only 3 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 4 tens and 13 ones. Ones: 13 − 8 = 5. Tens: 4 − 3 = 1. 53 − 38 = 15.

items.q: Some salmon were in a pool in the river. 15 more salmon swam in. Now there are 33. How many salmon were in the pool at first?
items.e: The whole is 33. One part is 15. Subtract. 33 has only 3 ones, so regroup: 2 tens and 13 ones. 13 − 5 = 8. 2 − 1 = 1. 33 − 15 = 18. Check: 18 + 15 = 33.

items.q: There are 46 people at the book fair. 19 people go home. Then 25 more people come. How many people are at the book fair now?
On a rainy day in Vancouver, 38 students wear rain boots and 27 students wear running shoes. How many students is that?
items.e: Find the total, so add. Tens: 30 + 20 = 50. Ones: 8 + 7 = 15. 15 ones is 1 ten and 5 ones. 50 + 15 = 65.

items.q: The book fair wants to sell 90 books today. It has sold 56 books. How many more books does it need to sell?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. 90 has 0 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 8 tens and 10 ones. Ones: 10 − 6 = 4. Tens: 8 − 5 = 3. 90 − 56 = 34.

items.q: For a field trip snack, the class has 26 apples and 34 granola bars. How many snacks is that in all?
items.e: In all means add. Tens: 20 + 30 = 50. Ones: 6 + 4 = 10. 10 ones is 1 ten and 0 ones. 50 + 10 = 60.

items.q: Kai counts 47 salmon. Ava counts 24 more salmon than Kai. How many salmon does Ava count?
items.e: Ava counts more, so add: 47 + 24. Tens: 40 + 20 = 60. Ones: 7 + 4 = 11. 60 + 11 = 71. (23 subtracts. 61 forgets to regroup.)

items.q: A BC Ferries boat gets to Nanaimo with 82 cars. 47 cars have driven off. How many cars are still on the boat?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. 82 has only 2 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 7 tens and 12 ones. Ones: 12 − 7 = 5. Tens: 7 − 4 = 3. 82 − 47 = 35.

items.q: Two classes count salmon at the creek. One class counts 64 salmon. The other class counts 36 salmon. How many salmon do they count in all?
items.e: The bar model shows two parts. Find the whole, so add. Tens: 60 + 30 = 90. Ones: 4 + 6 = 10. 10 ones is 1 ten and 0 ones. 90 + 10 = 100.

items.q: Harjot has 73 stickers. He gives away 36. Which number sentence finds how many are left?
items.e: He gives some away, so take away. Start with 73 and take away 36: 73 − 36 = ?. The answer is 37.

items.q: A school bus has 72 seats. 47 students are sitting down. How many seats are empty?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. 72 has only 2 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 6 tens and 12 ones. Ones: 12 − 7 = 5. Tens: 6 − 4 = 2. 72 − 47 = 25.

items.q: Nadia buys a book at the book fair. She reads 36 pages on Saturday and 47 pages on Sunday. How many pages does she read?
items.e: Put the two days together, so add. Tens: 30 + 40 = 70. Ones: 6 + 7 = 13. 13 ones is 1 ten and 3 ones. 70 + 13 = 83.
